prompt: A vertical 9:16 photograph of the corner of a three-storey 1970s brick council block in an English town, taken from across the street at eye level on a tripod with a normal lens, so the walls stand straight and the building fills almost the whole frame, with only a thin band of flat grey sky above the roofline. It is the very end of dusk under a heavy overcast sky: no sun, no shadows, the light so low and even that the maroon-brown stretcher-bond brick and the slate-grey sky sit almost at the same dull brightness. Concrete bands run along each floor. The windows are fat white uPVC casements with top-hung openers, and their frames pick up a faint violet-blue edge from the sky. Every window is dark except two on the first floor, either side of the corner: the left one glows a flat orange-amber through a drawn curtain with no detail visible, the right one shows cream vertical blinds with a single bare ceiling bulb burning behind them. The picture is soft and slightly smeared, as if shot through fine drizzle on a long exposure, with lifted blacks, low contrast and almost no colour except the warmth in those two windows. Quiet, still, nobody in the street. Thanks.
